clue.text: Hell's Angel's match

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the fallen angel who rules Hell, Satan
second meaning: an old word for a friction match

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a biker gang member's match or game; instead the clue joins Satan's name to an old trade name for a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Satan is called by this name as the fallen angel, and early friction matches were sold under the same name.

clue.text: Run to cut off drug

parts.note: to lop a branch is to cut it off

explanation.surface: Someone runs off to break with drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, loping stride is an easy running gait, so it is a synonym for run.

clue.text: French Marshal left Londoner for a bird

indicators.note: left as in departed, so the marshal's name goes out of the word

parts.note: a Cockney is a Londoner born within earshot of Bow bells
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: A French marshal abandoned a Londoner in favour of a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like the French marshal leaving someone, but it means he is taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: A male chicken or other male fowl is a bird, so the word names a specific bird.

clue.text: Ground fully occupied by hospital department that runs without a hitch

indicators.note: occupied by tells us the department is placed inside the reworked letters
ground as in crushed, so the letters of fully are broken up

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department

explanation.surface: A building fully taken over by a hospital unit that runs smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking or running smoothly with no hesitation is an idiomatic sense of doing something with no hitch.

clue.text: Concerning unknown journalist butting in shrilly

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, while the definition is an adverb describing a thin, high sound

indicators.note: butting in means pushing into, so the journalist goes inside

parts.note: an editor, ED, is a journalist

explanation.surface: An unknown reporter interrupts shrilly on some matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice that is thin and high, like a reed instrument, is described this way, close to a shrill quality.

clue.text: Poster modified to suit fast Italian

indicators.note: a poster modified has its letters changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A poster is altered to suit a quick-moving Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical tempo marking means very quick, so it is a fast instruction in Italian.

clue.text: Strangely, second best price fixed formula

indicators.note: strangely signals the letters fall into an odd new order
second takes the second letter of the word best

parts.note: the second letter of best is taken

explanation.surface: Oddly, the runner-up best price was decided by a set formula.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of instructions for cooking a dish is a standard procedure, a prescribed method.

clue.text: Substantial if, that is, first dish is set

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of dish

explanation.surface: Substantial, that is, if the first dish has set.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has hardened from a liquid to a firm state is set, as a jelly sets.

clue.text: Unsold hat I knitted was extraordinary

indicators.note: knitting works strands into a new pattern, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The hat I knitted that did not sell was bizarre.
explanation.definitionFit: Something strange or bizarre and far from the ordinary is called outlandish, a synonym.

clue.text: Representations of ancient tribe on both sides of river

indicators.note: the tribe sits on both sides, so the river's name goes inside the tribe's name

parts.note: the Picts were a people of ancient Scotland
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Images depicting an ancient tribe living on both banks of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Picts were a people of early Scotland; the Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings, drawings and photographs are all images that represent a scene, a synonym in the plural.

clue.text: Old English clot teased big cat

indicators.note: teased in the sense of combed out or pulled apart, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An old English fool is mocked by a large wild cat.
explanation.walkthrough: A clot is British slang for a fool, which makes 'teased' look like mockery rather than rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: This spotted wildcat of the Americas is a medium-sized feline, loosely counted among the big cats.

clue.text: Old students of Milan University getting involved

indicators.note: involved as in tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Former students of a university in Milan are getting involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Graduates or former pupils of a school or university are its alumni, plural.

clue.text: Second person paid out after cyclone ruined work

indicators.note: after places the scrambled assistant-and-payment letters behind the storm's letters
a ruined cyclone has its letters wrecked into a new order

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for paid, as on a bill

indicators.note: out as in wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a second, as in a duel or boxing, is an assistant, an aide

explanation.surface: An assistant is paid off after a storm wrecked their labours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second person' looks like grammar's 'you', but a second is a helper, as in a duel; that helper and the paid letter are jumbled and placed after the jumbled storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A multi-volume reference book is a published work, the word's sense of a book or literary production.

clue.text: At risk, but I'm overcoming danger and being guided

indicators.note: in a down answer, overcoming puts the first part on top of the next

explanation.surface: I am at risk, but I'm defeating danger with guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcoming' reads as triumph over danger, but in a down clue it means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: Put in danger or jeopardy, at risk of harm, is the plain sense of the past participle.

clue.text: Badly contaminated on being removed to entrance

indicators.note: badly shows the letters are put together in a disordered way
being removed tells us the word on is taken out of the longer word

explanation.surface: Something badly contaminated is removed to the entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: The right or act of entering a place, as at a box office, is a synonym for entry or entrance.

clue.text: Between my two appearances, silly old Des was interfering

indicators.note: the scrambled name goes between the two copies of the word, splitting them

parts.note: the word my, read as ME, appears twice

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters are behaving foolishly and out of order

explanation.surface: Old Des, always poking into things, gets between me and myself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who meddles pokes into other people's affairs, an exact synonym for prying or interfering.

clue.text: Issue on the Web in fourteen lines

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another is placed above it, so the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: issue means offspring, here a son
a web is a net, a mesh of threads

explanation.surface: Someone publishes a short poem online, posting it on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a publication but means a child; 'the Web' looks like the internet but is just a net.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a poem of exactly fourteen lines, classically in iambic pentameter with a set rhyme scheme.

clue.text: Some uttered a brief adieu to a short-lived trend

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used, a run lying inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of brief and the start of adieu

explanation.surface: Someone says a quick goodbye to a passing craze.
explanation.walkthrough: The three letters straddle the end of brief and the start of adieu.
explanation.definitionFit: A craze that is popular for a moment and then forgotten is a fashion of brief duration.

clue.text: Undercoat cut up without new teacher

indicators.note: cut up as in chopped into pieces, so the letters are rearranged
without signals leaving a letter out

explanation.surface: A teacher scrapes off an undercoat, leaving it unrenewed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who educates is a teacher, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Priest has every little item initially

indicators.note: initially, applying to all three words, points to the opening letter of each

explanation.surface: A priest owns every small item.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel who raised the boy Samuel, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament he is the high priest at Shiloh, so the name is a specific example.

clue.text: Cruelty shown by many ravens

definitions.meaning: first meaning: harshness or lack of kindness
second meaning: the traditional collective noun for a group of ravens

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a single image of menacing birds, but the second half is the old collective noun for ravens.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh behaviour is the plain sense, and a flock of these black birds is traditionally named the same way.

clue.text: Party colours

definitions.meaning: first meaning: members of the Green Party, as a political group
second meaning: various shades of the colour green

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the clue suggests the colours of a political party; the two words are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Environmental party members are known by the colour's plural, and shades of that hue also share the name.

clue.text: In time, dodgy reference leads to obstruction

indicators.note: a dodgy reference is unreliable, so its letters are shaken into another order

explanation.surface: Eventually, a dubious job reference ends up blocking someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindering or getting in the way, as in sport where a player blocks an opponent, is a synonym.

clue.text: Push aside the Spanish to receive applause

parts.note: a performer bows when receiving applause

explanation.surface: A Spaniard pushes others aside to collect the applause.
explanation.definitionFit: To shove someone out of the way with one's arm joint is to jostle them aside.

clue.text: Sound equipment initially hidden in first in-tray

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each following word

parts.note: the opening letters of hidden, in and first

explanation.surface: Some stereo gear was tucked away at first in an in-tray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' looks like a signal to find letters inside a word, but here it is one of the words whose initials are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for high fidelity, it names audio equipment that reproduces music faithfully.

clue.text: A fish used in seaweed preparation

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A fish is used in a preparation made from seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: This jelly extracted from red algae is a substance used in labs and cooking, made from marine plants.

clue.text: Creditor left finale with monarch

parts.note: the finale is the end of a show
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A creditor departs at the finale with a king or queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lends money is owed it, which is the meaning of a creditor.

clue.text: Article on gambling being helpful to principal performer

parts.note: betting on horses or games is gambling

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about gambling helps out a leading actor.
explanation.walkthrough: The principal is the legal term for the person who commits a crime, not a star of the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Abetting in law is helping or encouraging the perpetrator of an offence, an accomplice's role.

clue.text: Stylish attire finally ready

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of ready

explanation.surface: A smart outfit is at last prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that are smart and elegant, suited to a formal occasion, are called this.

clue.text: Soldier fighting near city — second in Brazil

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a city in Brazil

indicators.note: second in takes the second letter of the word Brazil

explanation.surface: A soldier in combat close to a Brazilian city.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighting man, especially a brave one, is a near synonym for a soldier.
